config.text: Studio product photograph, top-down, of one single tall narrow vertical menu card, very elongated proportion of 10 by 21 centimetres, lying flat and centred on a pale warm grey linen tablecloth, soft even daylight, the whole card visible with margin around it. The card is thick uncoated deep burgundy cotton paper, colour sang-de-boeuf #560002. The only printing is hot-foil stamping in two flat layers: underneath, a salmon in flat opaque matte white foil; on top, a lamb in flat bright silver metallic foil, printed over the white and fully opaque where they overlap. Each foil is one perfectly uniform solid area with crisp edges and a slight debossed relief in the paper. Drawing language of contemporary independent illustration posters: bold flat silhouettes, a few confident cut lines inside the shapes that reveal the burgundy paper, each cut line at least as thick as a pencil stroke; wild, expressive, slightly menacing creatures with dynamic twisted bodies, sharp and adult, with dry humour. The card carries no lettering. Relationship and composition: one chimera: a lamb whose body ends in a long salmon tail that curls into a large loop at the bottom of the card. The lamb's head, front legs and woolly body are silver; the long fish tail and fins are white and pass behind the lamb's legs. Rough dry-brush silhouette edges, flame-like wool tufts, crouching, devilish pose.
